title: The gathering
hook: all people gathered on one plain

segments.voice: Yesterday, the trumpet, blown twice, and your line: all will rise. Did standing up from a chair remind you once? Today, where everyone who rises goes. Day one thousand two hundred fifty-seven.

No skyline. No street signs. No tree to meet under, no house to point at, no hill to climb for a better view. A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari describes the ground of the Day of Resurrection like that: a white land, tinged with red, like a round loaf of fine flour, with no landmark on it belonging to anyone. Flat, open, and nobody's property. On that plain, the Qur'an says, every person will stand. Today, the gathering.
screen: `NO SKYLINE, NO SIGNS.` → `A LAND LIKE A LOAF OF FINE FLOUR.` → `NO LANDMARK FOR ANYONE.`

segments.voice: The Arabic is al-hashr, the gathering, and the Day is sometimes called yawm al-hashr. Surah al-Kahf says Allah will gather them and leave not one of them behind. Not one. All of them, on the same flat ground. And notice what's missing on that plain. In this life people gather by something: a city, a team, a language, a family name, a mosque, a church. Here, the hadith says, there's no landmark for anyone. No one's corner. No one's side of town. The Qur'an adds that each will come alone, as they were first created. Another hadith in Bukhari makes it even plainer. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said people will be gathered barefoot, unclothed, as they were born. 'A'ishah, his wife, heard it and asked the obvious question: men and women, looking at one another? And he answered, in paraphrase: the matter will be too serious for them to care about that. Everything people usually notice about each other, clothes, status, looks, is gone, and so is the urge to notice it. What's left is a person, and what they did. So the gathering is two things at once. It is a crowd with no one missing, all together on one plain. And each person in it stands alone, coming as they were made. The teaching holds both at once, and the next days of this part follow what happens on that plain.
screen: `AL-HASHR: LEAVE NOT ONE BEHIND.` · `NO LANDMARK, NO ONE'S CORNER.` · `TOO SERIOUS TO CARE ABOUT THAT.` · then, large: `ALL TOGETHER, AND EACH ALONE.`

segments.voice: The practice: picture everyone. Settle, and breathe. Start with the people closest to you: your family, the people you live with. Set them on a wide, flat, pale plain. Then add the people you saw today, the stranger in line, the driver, the neighbor. Then people from far away, people from history, people you've argued with. Keep adding until the plain is full, with no landmarks, no sides. Stand among them. Notice that nothing marks you out. If you pray, you can ask for mercy for all of them, in whatever words your tradition uses. If not, simply look at the crowd with kindness. The bell holds the time.
The gathering. Al-hashr: everyone raised and brought together on one plain on the Day of Resurrection, leaving not one behind. Today's word.

Your line: all together. Today, in one crowd, a bus, a store, a waiting room, look around once and remember that everyone in it will stand on the same plain. Tomorrow, the book in hand. Day one thousand two hundred fifty-seven.

howItsDone: Muslims believe all people will be raised and gathered for judgment on the Day of Resurrection; teachers sometimes point to the crowds of the Hajj at Arafat, all in plain white, as a reminder of that gathering.

fork.setup: you're 'A'ishah. you've just heard people will be gathered unclothed, as they were born. what do you do?
options: stay quiet and hope you misheard.
ask: men and women, looking at one another?
fork.reveal: she asked the obvious question, and the answer was that the matter would be too serious for anyone to care about that.

original.note: Arabic: the gathering; yawm al-hashr, the Day of Gathering.

trapdoor: what you thought: the gathering is a big crowd before judgment.
what it means: every person, leaving not one behind, on one flat plain with no one's landmark, each coming alone as first created.
what a scholar hears: al-hashr, the land like a loaf of fine flour, and 'A'ishah's question answered: too serious to care.
recall: the hereafter, the life that comes last

sources.ref: Qur'an 18:47 (We gather them and leave not one behind)

notes: All Qur'an references paraphrased; confirm 18:47 and 6:94.
Sahih al-Bukhari 6521 and 6527: confirm numbers and the paraphrase ('a white land tinged with red, like a round loaf of fine flour').
'All together, and each alone' is the writer's framing of 18:47 and 6:94; confirm.
